root_idea.summary: The root centers on breadth, spaciousness, and the extensive spread of water or other things.
root_idea.development: From the idea of widening or spreading come the meanings of a sea or large body of water, ranging widely in pasture, wealth, or knowledge, and figurative abundance. Related developments include salinity and the wide slitting of an animal's ear.

qac_form_accounting.reason: A distinct Quran-attested lexical noun referring to the pre-Islamic consecrated animal.
The principal Quran-attested noun for a sea or extensive body of water.

senses.definition: A consecrated animal, especially a she-camel whose ear had been slit and which was released from ordinary use under pre-Islamic custom.
senses.usage_conditions: The term could also apply to an ewe or she-goat. Accounts differ over whether the animal followed five, seven, or ten births and over the precise restrictions on riding, carrying, milk, meat, and pasture; the Quran rejects the institution in 5:103.

senses.definition: A sea or other extensive body of water; in a Quranic pairing, both salt and fresh bodies of water can be called seas.
senses.usage_conditions: The noun occurs in singular, dual, and plural forms and in descriptions of ordinary seas, paired waters, and vast or overwhelming waters.

senses.definition: A watered or cultivated region, settled country, or riverside towns.
senses.usage_conditions: This is the Quran-attested interpretive use of al-bahr in the expression al-barr wa-al-bahr in 30:41, where it is explained as fertile or watered countryside, settlements, or towns along rivers rather than the open sea alone.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To slit, cleave, or divide lengthwise; especially to slit an animal's ear widely.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The ear-slitting use underlies the noun بَحِيرَةٌ, but the verb may describe cutting or cleaving more generally.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become wide or spacious.
To embark or voyage upon the sea or a great river.
Of water, to become salty and difficult or unpleasant to drink.
Of land, to abound in places where water stagnates.
To meet someone unintentionally.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This meaning is reported in connection with the phrase لَقِيتُهُ صَحْرَةَ بَحْرَةَ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To range widely or become abundant in pasture, wealth, or knowledge; to become deeply versed in a field.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction may describe a pastor ranging through abundant grazing, a person becoming ample in wealth or possessions, or someone extending deeply into knowledge.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become wide or expanded; figuratively, to expatiate or become diffuse in speech.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The verb is used of places that spread widely and of a poet, speaker, or orator who ranges expansively in expression.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A great river whose water flows continuously.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term can be applied to major sweet-water rivers as well as to the sea.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In an idiom, a sea-like night associated with destruction or the approach of daybreak.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is the figurative expression يَا هَادِيَ اللَّيْلِ جُرْتَ إِنَّمَا هُوَ البَحْرُ أَوِ الفَجْرُ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Salt water; salty as an epithet applied to water.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a tropical or descriptive use distinguishing saline water from fresh water.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person or thing exceptionally wide-ranging or abundant: a swift far-ranging horse, a generous man, or a man of extensive knowledge.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The noun is used metaphorically for breadth in running, generosity, knowledge, or another capacity.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The bottom or fundus of the womb.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The anatomical term is also shortened to البَحْرُ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A broad tract of land, an open valley, or low and depressed ground.
A country, territory, town, or village, especially one associated with running water or wholesome water.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The word may refer broadly to a people's land or settlement and is also used of towns and villages.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A meadow or garden, especially one that is broad or spacious.
A place where water stagnates.
Face-to-face and out in the open, with nothing intervening or concealing either party.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The expression functions as an idiom of meeting in an exposed, unobstructed situation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of, relating to, or belonging to the sea or a great river.
A seaman or sailor.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The same derived form can function as a noun for a person associated with the sea.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In the Egyptian dialect, northern or northward.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This regional directional use is attributed to the position of the Mediterranean Sea relative to Egypt.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The crisis or sudden turning point of an acute disease, including the beginning of recovery or a change for better or worse.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a post-classical medical term associated in the cited discussion with a fixed stage of illness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Menstrual or womb blood, especially blood described as abundant, thick, or intensely red.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term is variously related to the bottom of the womb or to the abundance of the blood; the source records several traditional specifications.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Intensely red.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This adjectival use may describe redness apart from the specific reference to menstrual or womb blood.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A small sea or lake.
The intense heat of the month of Tammuz, approximately July.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The feminine form بَاحُورَاءُ is used with the same meaning.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The moon.

cautions: The interpretation of al-bahr in Quran 30:41 varies between the literal sea and extended senses such as fertile regions, settlements, or towns beside rivers.
Descriptions of the pre-Islamic bahirah custom differ in the reported number of births and in the restrictions imposed on the animal.
